memories.content: Avoid em dashes in the proposal; split the sentence or use more ordinary punctuation instead.
The user tends to place several independently reviewable claims in one long sentence.
Use first-person active voice for choices and commitments owned by the proposal author so responsibility remains explicit throughout the work plan.
Describe prototype operations that have already been implemented and verified as observed states.
Describe prototype operations not yet implemented or evaluated as plans or expectations.
When a commitment is phrased passively, readers may interpret it as uncertainty, evasiveness, or reluctance to take responsibility.
Use “we” only for decisions and commitments the authors control, not for external facts or actions owned by another party.
The user should use one first-person pronoun consistently for the same authorial role and should not alternate between “I” and “we” unless the responsible party actually changes.
The user tends to hide unsettled commitments behind passive phrases such as “will be considered” or “is expected.”
Split proposal prose into short sentences when a sentence contains more than one independently reviewable claim.
Keep one main claim in each sentence so a reviewer can locate and assess it quickly.
The user tends to repeat em dashes when a sentence already contains several clauses.
Repeated em dashes can shift a reviewer’s attention from the proposal’s argument to suspicion that its prose was generated by AI.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate domains: proposal-writing style and evidentiary phrasing on one side, participant-compensation policy on the other. Neither supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims, so the ledger preserves each independently useful policy cluster without treating absence as disagreement.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories jointly state a writing tendency, its corrective policy, and its reviewer-facing rationale; the compared frame contains no corresponding prose-style claim.
relations.summary: Proposal prose should avoid repeated em dashes, especially in clause-heavy sentences, because they can distract reviewers and suggest AI-generated writing.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories describe one sentence-density tendency and its unified corrective principle; the compared frame contains no corresponding sentence-structure policy.
relations.summary: Proposal sentences should be shortened so each contains one independently reviewable main claim.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories state one accountability problem, its consequence, and its corrective voice policy; the compared frame contains no corresponding authorship-voice claim.
relations.summary: Author-owned choices and commitments should use explicit first-person active voice rather than passive wording that obscures responsibility.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-side rule governing the ownership scope of “we,” with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Use “we” only for author-controlled decisions and commitments, not for external facts or another party’s actions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-side consistency rule distinct from determining whether “we” is authorized, and the compared frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Keep the first-person pronoun consistent for a stable authorial role, changing between “I” and “we” only when responsibility changes.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one status-sensitive representation policy across explicit implementation conditions; the compared frame contains no corresponding prototype-description claim.
relations.summary: Describe verified prototype operations as observed states and unimplemented or unevaluated operations as plans or expectations.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories state the principle, fairness basis, modality consequence, and recurring omission pattern of one burden-based compensation policy; the reference frame contains no compensation counterpart.
relations.summary: Set and differentiate participant compensation according to total participation burden, including session time, travel, technical preparation, and commonly omitted setup or follow-up work.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories state one actual-time payment rule and its withdrawal application; the reference frame contains no corresponding compensation claim.
relations.summary: Compensate actual session participation time across modalities, including when a participant withdraws midway.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side payment alternative with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Remote participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive gift cards of equivalent value.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side proposal-assessment policy with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method should not be treated as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side rule for a specific recurring study burden not expressly covered by the other compensation relations or the reference frame.
relations.summary: Compensation for longitudinal studies should include time spent on diary entries and repeated reporting outside sessions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side cost-classification boundary with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Participant research compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as job duties.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers burden-based participant compensation, partial participation, payment methods, modality differences, longitudinal reporting, and separation of participant payments from staff labor costs.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers sentence structure, em-dash avoidance, accountable first-person voice, pronoun ownership and consistency, and status-sensitive descriptions of prototype operations.
